newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-ITALIAN WOMAN HAS BEST TRAINING RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ITALIAN WOMAN HAS BEST TRAINING RUN.

text.p: Isolde Kostner of Italy battled gusting winds to post the fastest time during Wednesday's opening training run for the women's World Cup downhill.

Kostner was timed in 1:50.52, one-tenth of a second faster than Stefanie Schuster of Austria. Hilary Lindh of the United States was third in 1:51.07 and another Austrian, Alexandra Meissnitzer, fourth in 1:51.38.

Picabo Street of the United States, reigning world champion and two-time World Cup downhill winner, fell hard on the steep finishing face and suffered an undetermined injury to her knee. Ski patrolmen carried her off on a toboggan to be examined at a local hospital.
Overnight snow softened the course and slowed speeds.

"It seemed easy, much easier than in previous years," said Katja Seizinger, who won the season downhill opener last week at Lake Louise, Canada, and had the eighth-fastest training time on Wednesday. "Of course that all can change with course conditions."
Seizinger, the defending overall champion, has won twice at Vail, in 1992 and 1994.
